description: Committee recommends dedicated bus lanes for 1st Avenue Link.
This includes a minor traffic lane change at 24th Street.
Committee also requested a public art plan for the project.

chips.text: Recommended
$75,000 of $500,000 public art budget already spent.
Councillor Jeffries argued more mixed traffic would not ruin BRT.
Midtown Plaza and Bus Riders of Saskatoon support dedicated lanes.
Questions remain about Capital Music Club's alley access for loading.
Businesses expressed concerns about reduced parking and traffic congestion.
Some councillors preferred a hybrid option or Option 3 for business balance.
Changes to dedicated lanes could impact iCIP funding agreements.
Accessibility Advisory Committee requested dedicated consultation for disabled community.

speakers.name: Cary Tarasoff
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: 1st Avenue Bus Rapid Transit (Link) Concept Changes Follow Up _Redacted1
said: BRT is reliable, not rapid; buses don't go faster.
Traffic modeling is flawed; patterns already changed.
Snow removal plan is inadequate; needs daytime clearing.

speakers.name: Bruno Bartel
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: 1st Ave BRT (Link) Concept Changes Follow-Up
said: Supports rapid bus route with dedicated lanes.
Modern transit essential for Midtown's vibrancy and accessibility.
Long-term benefits outweigh short-term disruptions.

speakers.name: Curt McCoshen
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: 1st Ave BRT Concept
said: Fully supports administration's current plans for improvement.
Many people need and would use better public transit.
Transit should be seen as an essential service.

speakers.name: Sherry Tarasoff
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: 1st Ave BRT Concept
said: Traffic analysis has not considered the Downtown Event and Entertainment District.
Concerns about 1st Avenue platforms accommodating multiple transit lines.
Delay approval to test College Drive BRT first.

speakers.name: Keith Moen
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: 1st Ave BRT Concept
said: Supports improved public transit and Link objectives.
Recommends a blended Option 3 (20th-23rd) and Option 2 (23rd-25th).
Option 3 offers flexibility for emergency vehicles and minor collisions.

speakers.name: Shawna Nelson
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: 1st Ave BRT Concept
said: Supports progress, investment, and better public transit.
System must function in practice for downtown users.
Blended approach is a step forward, but curbside/dedicated signals should be explored.

description: Committee recommends 2024-2026 collective agreement with IAFF Local 80.
Includes annual wage increases and extends 24-hour shift pilot.
Addresses firefighter health and dental benefit changes.

chips.text: Recommended
Annual wage increases ranging from 3% to 4.5% are included.
Administration may put province on notice to withdraw paramedic service.
The agreement affects 346 members of IAFF Local 80.
Unclear how new fire halls will be fully staffed without thinning resources.
IAFF Local 80 members approved contract with only 66% due to frustration.
Administration will report back in Q1 2027 on SHA negotiations.

speakers.name: Jay Protz
speakers.organization: The International Association of Fire Fighters, Local No. 80
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Contract Ratification
said: Supports contract settlement, but members frustrated with 66% approval.
Saskatoon fire service is superior, deserves better recognition and wages.
New fire halls thin resources, stressing service due to overdose crisis.
